The pairs that look like duplicates are Git bin->usr bash wrapper parents, so there is no race. Arithmetic with d_P = 0.956: A-M2 = exp89s iff d_R >= 0.960. The main session's text is correct. Three items must be logged BEFORE exp89r's first terminal header (earliest plausible ~09:05Z, expected 09:20-09:35Z). (1) The 07:59Z sentence 'SEC files cannot be V_pub unless another file beats 0.959' contradicts Q3 and the card's pool rule. (2) The running-champion tie order (1) inverts its own rationale when the champion is the SEC file exp89r and a later SEC-free exp89s ties it. In that band exp89s would read 0.960 and displace exp87a, but exp89r reads only 0.959. The slot costs nothing (2 of 5 left, and they expire at 23:59Z). The cleanest variant is conditional: send exp89s iff d_R >= 0.959, pre-registered before the read and with the user's yes. The private value is small, because exp89s as V_pub trades CI for DIS. Smaller items: A-M2 step 1 has no 10:50:28Z admit edge; there are exp89s logistics (probe label, PENDING window, a fresh S0 after the e10 loop stops at 12:00Z, a late-read push through 23:59Z); and the stale 08:30Z timer.

findings.what: The 07:59Z read line ends: 'SEC files (exp89p, exp89r, exp89l, exp89q) cannot be V_pub unless another file beats 0.959 - not applicable.' That contradicts the logged finals rules. Q3 (28 Sep 11:26Z) says a SEC file may be a final ONLY as V_pub. Card v5 l.17 and fill step 5 take V_pub as the max display among COMPLETE files in the pool, under order (1), with no SEC exclusion. The freeze (9) clause '0 or - removes SEC from every morning file' covers morning SUBMITS, not the finals pool. Read literally, the 07:59Z sentence would drop exp89r from V_pub even if it reads 0.960+ (or 0.959 with an attributable UP). The card would then keep exp87a against the logged pool rule. The two readings differ in exactly the cases where exp89r's read is actionable, so the sentence must be resolved before that read, not after.

The card's SEC line shows SEC_READ = - (0.956) next to any SEC V_pub.' The alternative, excluding SEC files from V_pub after SEC '-', is a rule change. It is legitimate ONLY if it is logged before exp89r's read and states its consequence: exp89r >= 0.960 would then leave V_pub = exp87a. Pick one; do not leave the ambiguous sentence as the only text.

findings.what: The running-champion tie order (02:02Z (2), card v5 order (1)) gives the wrong answer in a reachable branch. Suppose exp89r reads >= 0.960. It becomes champion (V_pub, 5 levers: cap 6, K, SEC, DIS, CI), and A-M2 sends exp89s (K + DIS, 3 levers, no SEC, no CI), which reads ~16:20-17:30Z. If exp89s ties exp89r's display with k = 0 / MASKED / BLIND, order (1) keeps exp89r. The same holds if exp89r = 0.959 with an attributable UP (champion) and a later exp89s ties at 0.959. The 02:02Z rationale was 'CI has two LB + reads, SEC a weak negative prior'. Here the LB itself gives E[exp89r - exp89s] = CI + SEC ~ +0.001 - 0.002 = -0.001 on the public embryo. At an equal display the SEC-free file is expected HIGHER unrounded, and orders (2) non-CI and (3) fewer levers also pick exp89s. The conservative reading keeps, as the final, the file carrying the one lever with a direct negative LB read.
findings.evidence: CONTEXT.md l.4278-4285 (02:02Z (2) rationale); l.4394-4403 (SEC -0.002 on the K base); card v5 l.21-24 and fixed_refs (exp87a UP 12 vs 0.958); levers list step 5 (exp89r = 5, exp89s = 3). Unrounded bounds: CI = exp87a - exp85a in (0, 0.002), SEC = exp89p - exp85a in (-0.003, -0.001).
findings.action: Log a narrow tie clause BEFORE exp89r's read (it is still pre-score for both exp89r and exp89s): 'ORDER (1) EXCEPTION (post SEC '-', 07:59Z): if the running champion carries SEC and a later SEC-free file reaches the SAME display, the SEC-free file replaces it without an UP test (orders (2)-(3) decide); a SEC champion keeps V_pub only against files it strictly beats.' No other change: exp87a vs any later file keeps the conservative reading. If the session prefers not to change order (1), then at the 12:03Z / 18:37Z fill put an info line under V_pub whenever V_pub is a SEC file and a SEC-free file ties it: '<SEC-free file> has the same public score and no SEC (SEC read on LB: -0.002); by order (1) the main file stays <SEC file>'. The user then sees the trade.

findings.what: Input for the user's pending question (exp89s now as a clean DIS test). After SEC '-', the A-M2 gate (d_R >= 0.960) has lost power. Assuming additivity on the K base: d_R = exp87a + SEC + DIS. Reaching >= 0.9595 needs DIS > 0.9595 - exp87a - SEC, in (0.001, 0.004), central ~+0.0025. exp89s = exp85a + DIS reaches >= 0.9595 (the level that displaces exp87a) at DIS > (0.001, 0.002], central ~+0.0015. In the band DIS ~+0.0015..+0.0025, exp89r reads 0.959, A-M2 is UNUSED, yet exp89s would read 0.960 and become V_pub. In the same band, if exp89r's 0.959 earns an attributable UP, V_pub becomes exp89r, which carries SEC, while no SEC-free DIS file is ever tested. The slot cost is 0: A-M1 is UNUSED, 2 of 5 slots are left and they expire at 23:59Z. Sending exp89s now also spends the slot when d_R <= 0.958 (DIS likely <= +0.001). In that case its read can only matter through a +0.001 display that contradicts exp89r. That is a noise-driven V_pub flip which swaps CI (2 LB '+' reads, 7/8 lab clips) for DIS (lab ~0: -0.0008 on exp70g, +0.0004 on exp89p). The private value is small in every variant, because exp89s as V_pub trades CI for DIS. The file that would test DIS without dropping CI (exp89t, K + DIS + CI) is not built (default no; R8).

findings.action: Put three options to the user in one message, and take the answer only if it is timestamped BEFORE exp89r's first terminal header. (a) DEFAULT: follow the rule (exp89s iff d_R >= 0.960). (b') RECOMMENDED if the user wants a DIS test: exp89s iff d_R >= 0.959 (dd >= +0.002, i.e. drop only the 'exp89r > max(exp87a, exp89p)' winners clause), decided at exp89r's terminal header and submitted then (read ~16:20-17:30Z). (b) Send now: acceptable, since the slot is free, but it adds the noise-flip case above. Whichever is chosen, log it as a pre-registered line before the header, with the user's words and time. If the user answers only after exp89r's header, log that the answer came after the read, and present the read with it. Do not apply (b) silently at that point, because it would be conditioning on d_R.
